New: live visuals while a review runs, a pull request list you can search, group and pin, and a one-line hand-off of your own pull request's fixes to your coding chat.

What's new

- Live review visuals: a strip of the steps with a fact under each, one tile per reviewer and chunk (waiting, running, done), a file map with one square per changed file that fills as reviewers open it, a heartbeat and running counters. With Reduce Motion on, the pulses stand still.
- Finding a pull request: a search box in the review window's sidebar (⌘F). Without a search, To review is split into Needs you, Reviewing now, Waiting on author and Approved by you; each group folds.
- Pinned and Recent: pin a pull request from its row (or P) to keep it at the top until it is merged or declined. Recent lists the last 5 opened.
- Copy for chat (⌘⇧C), on your own pull requests: copies one line that points your coding chat at a local fix list. The list holds the findings you have not ticked Done, each with file, line and suggested fix, and the open comments from other people with their replies. The comments are re-read from Bitbucket first. It says so when the pull request has new commits since the review.
- Comments from others: a read-only list on your own pull request, with a refresh. It is there before any review has run, so other people's comments alone can be handed over.

Limits

- A comment is tagged as a bot when Bitbucket marks the account as an app or its name contains "bot". Other bots show as a person; their comments are in the fix list either way.
- Nothing is posted, approved or resolved from your own pull request's page.

Install or upgrade:

    brew install --cask ankeshshankar/tap/ai-notch
    brew upgrade --cask ai-notch

After upgrading, the app is signed ad hoc, so macOS forgets Microphone, Input Monitoring and Accessibility: remove AI Notch from each list in System Settings → Privacy & Security, add it again, then quit and reopen the app.

First open: the app is signed ad hoc and not notarized, so macOS blocks it once. Open AI Notch, then in System Settings → Privacy & Security click Open Anyway and confirm with your password. If Set Up then reports the helper is blocked, run the command it shows:

    xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/AINotch.app

Requires macOS 15 or later (dictation: macOS 26).
